Vaelthoron — God of the ancient wilds, he demands no prayers, only silence among old trees.
Morgathur — God of death and decay, his priests are welcome everywhere and trusted nowhere.
Zenobia — Goddess of righteous war, patron of those who fight for something worth dying for.
Khorvath — God of blood and conquest, worshipped by those who call their appetites destiny.
Lysandra — Moon goddess of secrets, she lights the way for thieves, lovers, and those who are both.
Thromos — God of storms and the merciless deep, he does not hear prayers from drowning sailors.
Seraphina — Goddess of mercy and healing, her temples are the only places enemies may share bread without weapons drawn.
Zephyrus — God of wind and wandering, patron of sailors, merchants, and everyone with something to run from.
Kaelen — God of fate and the unseen thread, his followers believe every death was already written.
Nyxaria — Goddess of the night sky and hidden knowledge, her cult meets only after dark and discusses nothing with outsiders.
Yvaine — Goddess of starlight and fortune, consulted before every voyage and every gamble worth making.
Gorst — God of labor and endurance, patron of miners, soldiers, and everyone who suffers without complaining about it.
Elowen — Goddess of harvest and the turning seasons, she demands honesty from soil and those who work it.
Ignis — God of fire and the forge, patron of smiths and those who believe destruction makes room for something better.
Solaria — Goddess of the sun and divine order, her church wields more political power than most monarchs dare admit.
Tenebris — God of shadow and cold silence, neither death exactly nor darkness precisely, but something quieter than both.
Astraea — Goddess of celestial justice, blind to rank and rumored to be equally blind to mercy.
Sylas — God of the hunt and the wild edge, claimed equally by poachers and game wardens, which says everything.

tables.name: Lifepath · What Happened to Your Parents (1C)

results.description: They were slain by a rampaging dragon who still lives high in the mountains. Or perhaps deep in a forbidden swamp.
They vanished during a magical experiment gone wrong involving a portal to another plane. They may still be alive.
Your parents died in a battle. You never received the bodies and do not know where they were buried.
They were executed after being falsely accused of treason against the crown. They are still in prison.
They made a pact with a powerful fiend and were claimed when the contract came due. The fiend still owns their souls.
They are alive but cursed—transformed into animals, statues, or shadows. They are somewhere in an enchanted forest.
They disappeared while exploring ancient ruins that scholars believe is the lair of a lich. They may still be in there.
One parent died in a battle, betrayed by a beloved friend. The other is overwhelmed by grief.
They were lost at sea during a violent storm stirred by a wrathful sea god. The ship returned to shore without a crew.
They abandoned you to join a secretive order of assassins. They are still alive out there.
They were turned into undead and now wander as wights or revenants.
They are imprisoned in a distant land for crimes they may, or may not, have committed.
They were taken by the Fey after offending the Autumn Queen. They still serve her, hand and foot, to this day.
They died protecting you from a marauding band of mercenaries. The mercenary captain spared you for some reason. You don’t know why.
They were kidnapped by cultists of the Spider Queen. They are still there as bonded servants.
They were heroes who fell battling a vampire lord or lady. They are probably still there, serving the vampire.
They are alive and well, but you fled home after a bitter falling out. You are still reluctant to go home.
They were erased from existence by a powerful wish spell gone awry. The wish came from a magic ring, owned by an evil wizard, that can reverse the spell.
They were petrified by a gorgon, and their statues still stand somewhere.
They secretly rule a hidden criminal empire—and you’ve only just learned the truth.
